research_mode: official ONS, Home Office and Police.uk web sources only; current methodology, statistical status, force and neighbourhood identifier scope, date-specific categories, approximate-location semantics, outcomes maturity, current release edition and property-to-geography lookup guards; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Crime in England and Wales QMI
verified_claims: last revised 2 April 2026
the main sources are the Crime Survey for England and Wales and police recorded crime
neither source provides a complete count of crime and each has exclusions
police recorded crime is supplied through the Home Office by 43 territorial forces plus British Transport Police
limitations: the QMI is methodology and quality evidence rather than a parcel observation
source complementarity does not justify combining unlike measures without preserving definitions and geography

sources.name: Crime in England and Wales QMI quality characteristics
verified_claims: police recorded crime covers notifiable offences reported to and recorded by police and excludes non-notifiable offences such as anti-social behaviour
around 42 percent of CSEW-comparable crimes were reported to police in the year ending March 2025, with variation by offence
police records are continuously updated and quarterly snapshots can include revisions, transfers, cancellations and category changes
limitations: reporting proportions are not parcel-specific
a quarterly or monthly snapshot must remain edition-pinned and is not immutable incident truth

sources.name: Action plan for improving the quality of police recorded crime statistics
verified_claims: last revised 3 February 2025
the plan responds to Office for Statistics Regulation recommendations
the plan treats CSEW and police recorded crime as sources with different strengths and limitations
limitations: an action plan describes intended quality improvements and is not evidence that every action is complete
it does not supply parcel-level data

sources.name: User guide to crime statistics for England and Wales: March 2025
verified_claims: police recorded crime covers a wider offence and victim population than CSEW but does not capture all crime
the National Crime Recording Standard introduced in April 2002 changed recording levels and the main trend focus is from year ending March 2003
records are entered and updated continuously while investigations proceed
quality checks occur across capture, force validation, Home Office collation and publication
limitations: recording consistency does not establish exact location accuracy
trend breaks and live revisions must be preserved in any derived comparison

sources.name: Crime and justice methodology
verified_claims: last revised 9 June 2026
the index links current user guides, methodological notes, questionnaires and assessment material
current methodology includes the user guide, QMI, quality action plan and source-finding guidance
limitations: an index confirms document currency and relationships but does not add a crime observation
superseded documents must not override current guidance

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: List of forces API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns force identifiers and names available through the API
British Transport Police is excluded from the returned force list
force identifiers are used for force-specific API methods
limitations: absence from this list does not prove absence from all crime records
a force identifier is not a statistical geography or parcel identifier

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: List of neighbourhoods for a force API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint lists neighbourhood identifiers and names for a selected force
a neighbourhood identifier is force-specific
the same identifier may be used by a different force
limitations: neighbourhood IDs require the force context to be unique
police neighbourhoods are operational areas and are not interchangeable with LSOAs

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Specific neighbourhood API contract
verified_claims: the response can include a neighbourhood centre point, population, contact details and associated locations
the documented centre point may not be exactly in the centre
the identifier remains force-specific and may be reused by another force
limitations: the centre point is not a geometric boundary or parcel location
the population field is not a substitute for an edition-pinned ONS LSOA denominator

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Neighbourhood boundary API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns latitude and longitude pairs forming a police neighbourhood boundary
the boundary is requested with force and neighbourhood identifiers
limitations: an operational police neighbourhood boundary is not an ONS statistical boundary
it must not replace the official 2021 LSOA point-in-polygon join

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Crime categories API contract
verified_claims: the endpoint returns valid crime categories for a specified dataset date
each category has a URL identifier and human-readable name
the all-crime category includes crime and anti-social behaviour
limitations: category availability and labels must be pinned to the requested month
all-crime must not be treated as a homogeneous notifiable-crime measure

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Crimes at a location API contract
verified_claims: a location ID query returns crimes mapped to that predefined location
a latitude and longitude query finds the nearest predefined location rather than the exact supplied point
returned street names and coordinates are approximate
outcome_status provides the latest recorded outcome rather than a full history
limitations: nearest-location matching cannot prove that an incident occurred on the target parcel
the latest outcome is not the complete outcome sequence

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Street-level outcomes API contract
verified_claims: outcomes can be requested by location ID, one-mile point query or custom polygon and optional month
custom areas containing more than 10,000 outcomes return HTTP 503
crime locations in the response remain approximate
outcomes are not available for the Police Service of Northern Ireland
limitations: outcomes at an approximate point or area are contextual and not parcel outcomes
HTTP 503 requires bounded subdivision or explicit no-result handling rather than silent omission

sources.name: National Statistics UPRN Products
verified_claims: the National Statistics UPRN Lookup assigns current addresses to Output Areas using UPRN and point-in-polygon methodology
higher statistical geographies are then assigned through best-fit relationships using Census population data
the product is intended for National Statistics producers used with Ordnance Survey AddressBase
limitations: UPRN-to-OA point assignment and OA-to-higher-geography best fit are different operations
the product has eligibility and AddressBase dependencies and is not evidence that the current runtime parcel points have been joined

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Stop and searches by location API contract
verified_claims: stop-and-search records can be requested for a location ID and optional month
published stop-and-search locations are approximate rather than exact
the response describes search circumstances and outcomes rather than recorded-crime incidence
limitations: stop-and-search activity measures police activity and is not a crime count
approximate locations cannot be attributed to a parcel

sources.name: Crime outcomes in England and Wales 2025 to 2026
verified_claims: published 23 July 2026
the release covers police crime outcomes for the financial year ending March 2026
the publication includes official data tables, a technical annex and user-engagement material
limitations: national and force outcome statistics are not exact parcel observations
outcome timing and cohort definitions must be preserved when comparing rates

sources.name: Police recorded crime and outcomes open data tables and user guide
verified_claims: the open-data page was last updated 23 April 2026 and provides PFA, CSP, offence, outcomes, alternate-outcome, transferred-or-cancelled and supplementary products
the page supplies separate geographical and offence reference tables
the user guide states that outcomes linked to offences recorded in a quarter initially provide an incomplete picture because investigations may remain open
limitations: products with different geography, cohort and outcome definitions must not be merged without explicit keys
an initially incomplete outcome cohort must not be interpreted as a final clearance distribution
